findings.issue: The leaf's defining core has three required structures, including a fulfillment-to-event loop in which every sold benefit is an obligation with a delivery state and is tracked to event day. The cited README and docs/sales.rst establish sponsor/exhibitor records, sponsor groups, sponsorship/exhibition products, booth quotas and sold-out state, orders and payment, organization profiles, public pages, and lead scanning. They do not document per-benefit fulfillment/delivery tracking or a post-event value report. The batch's own match reason and service boundary acknowledge this gap, so the case currently evidences a sponsorship sales/inventory module rather than the full sponsor-management core.
findings.fix: Add an official source (documentation or repository code) showing benefit/asset delivery states and fulfillment-to-event tracking. If such evidence does not exist, replace the case with a sponsor-management product that demonstrates all three structures, or withdraw the sponsor-management match and record the leaf as lacking a verified case.

non_blocking_notes: festival-management: Eventree's homepage is strongest on accreditation, advancing, and on-site operations. The multi-venue, multi-day, recurring-edition festival object is implied by its festival clients and 'year after year' wording rather than explicitly described. This is acceptable for the commercial basic authenticity/type check, but the page should not be presented as proof of a full festival production suite.

speaker-management: Eventyay's README is a feature-level source ('Call for Participation workflows', 'Speaker, submission, review, and schedule management'). The organizer collection/coordination loop (profile and material tasks, completion tracking, reminders) is inferred from those features rather than shown in a workflow document. Adding the talks/speaker documentation would strengthen the case.

sponsor-management: eventyay-exhibition is a plugin that requires the eventyay host, not a standalone service. The batch discloses this dependency, so it is not a separate blocker, but the application scope should be read as an eventyay module.

attraction-management-system: ROLLER's page provides 'check-in via POS or mobile' and capacity management, but does not use explicit scan/redemption/attendance language. This is enough for a commercial basic type match, not a complete workflow proof.

attraction-ticketing: Gateway's page is a product feature page rather than detailed documentation. The described sales channels and admission-control hardware/API are nevertheless strong enough for the commercial basic check.
Cross-cutting: commercial entries were checked only for basic authenticity and type match. No pricing, deployment, or runtime validation was performed, consistent with the task scope.

festival-management.basis: The official homepage describes a web-based accreditation/advancing/operations system for festivals, tours, and other events. Organizers upload contacts, assign pass choices, approve accreditation requests, email unique QR codes for on-site collection, scan QR codes at check-in to issue passes/wristbands, and enforce inductions, documents, and ID checks. This supports the participant-ecosystem and access-entitlement structures, including the crew-facing form explicitly allowed by the leaf.
festival-management.service_form: Web application with annual per-event subscription pricing (Standard/Pro/Max), evidencing SaaS delivery.
festival-management.id_track: commercial:eventree with track commercial is consistent with the official homepage; no open-source license claim is made.
festival-management.gap: The page does not detail the festival as a multi-venue, multi-day, recurring-edition record. That is implied by festival clients and recurring-year language but not spelled out; non-blocking for a commercial basic check.

speaker-management.basis: The README states the platform provides Call for Participation workflows, speaker and session management, review and schedule management, and an organizer area for talks and speakers. This evidences persistent speaker records, binding to sessions/schedule, and organizer-side management. The leaf's collection/coordination loop is supported at feature level rather than by a detailed workflow document.
speaker-management.identity: GitHub repository id 62668744, full_name fossasia/eventyay; metadata description and README match.
speaker-management.license: The license snapshot is the full LICENSE file at ref dev (size 11358 bytes) and its content begins with the standard Apache License 2.0 text. The README states Apache-2.0 licensing and self-hosting. Hosted/enterprise support is mentioned, but no feature gating or additional restrictions are documented in the snapshots.
speaker-management.service_form: Self-hostable web application with Docker deployment and a hosted Eventyay service; satisfies the software service form.
speaker-management.gap: No direct documentation page was provided for speaker profile/material task tracking or reminders. The third leg is inferred from CFP, speaker management, and notification/scheduled-task features; a source with a concrete speaker workflow would strengthen the case.

sponsor-management.basis: README and docs/sales.rst document exhibitor/sponsor records, sponsor groups, sponsorship/exhibition products with price/category/availability/purpose/booth, booth quotas with sold-out state, orders and payment, organization profiles created from paid orders, public sponsor pages, and lead scanning. This strongly evidences the inventory and commitment structures.
sponsor-management.identity: GitHub repository id 111919967, full_name fossasia/eventyay-exhibition; metadata description matches the plugin role.
sponsor-management.license: The license snapshot is the full LICENSE file at ref dev (size 11357 bytes) and its content begins with the standard Apache License 2.0 text. README states Apache-2.0. No separate community/enterprise split or restricted-use clause is documented.
sponsor-management.service_form: Plugin for eventyay requiring the eventyay host; the dependency is disclosed in the batch, so this is a module of the eventyay service rather than a standalone service.
sponsor-management.gap: No documented per-benefit delivery state or fulfillment-to-event loop, and no post-event value report. The collector's own match reason and service boundary acknowledge this. Because the leaf treats the fulfillment loop as one of three constitutive structures, the case currently supports only a sponsorship sales/inventory module.

attraction-management-system.basis: The official zoo/aquarium page describes online ticketing, capacity management, check-in via POS or mobile, memberships and season passes, group bookings, POS, and add-ons for paid-entry venues. This supports operator-defined admission products, sale, and entry check-in at a commercial basic level.
attraction-management-system.service_form: Commercial SaaS platform for visitor attractions.
attraction-management-system.id_track: commercial:roller with track commercial is consistent with the official roller.software page.
attraction-management-system.gap: The page does not explicitly state that scan/redemption produces an attendance record. 'Check-in via POS or mobile' is the closest evidence; acceptable for the commercial basic type check, but not a full workflow proof.

attraction-ticketing.basis: The official Galaxy product page describes selling general, timed, unlimited-capacity, and limited-capacity tickets online, through distributors, hotels, on-site windows, kiosks, and the call center; passes and memberships; and admission control using barcodes, bracelets, turnstiles, self-serve gates, and mobile scanners. It also reports entrances, reentries, crossovers, and exits. This evidences the sell-issue-validate core.
attraction-ticketing.service_form: Commercial ticketing and admission-control software; hosting and managed services are offered.
attraction-ticketing.id_track: commercial:gateway-ticketing with track commercial is consistent with the official product page.
attraction-ticketing.gap: The page is a product feature page rather than detailed documentation, and no separate order/transaction object is described. The sales channels and admission control are sufficient for a commercial basic check.

limits: Read-only review of the specified snapshots only; no shell, no file writes, no deployment or runtime tests, and no external web, pricing, or architecture research. GitHub repository metadata snapshots are single long JSON lines and were partially truncated by the reader; repository IDs, full names, archived=false, and license-file size/header were verified from the available content, but the complete base64 license body was not decoded line-by-line. input.json progress fields appear to be pre-collection placeholders and were not used as evidence; batch.json and research.json were treated as the collection result. Commercial cases were assessed only for basic authenticity and type match.
